Are you up to the task? Sfynx is a solo/cooperative game for one to four players. You must solve 9 riddles by manipulating tiles on a 5x5 grid (called the Antechamber) so that the positions of the tiles match given patterns shown on the Riddle cards. You’ll only have a limited amount of turns, so you’ll need to make the best use of your actions. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary The Basics and Objective Objective Line up the Civilization tiles left to right or top to bottom to match the Riddle cards. Civilization tiles must be on their uncurled (light) side to match the Riddle cards. You gain a Reward card whenever a Riddle card is completed. Complete all 9 Riddle cards before the end of 12 rounds to beat the game. Game Play Carry out 2 basic and 1 special actions. Using Reward cards are optional. Completing a Riddle card does not cost an action. At the end of a round, a Challenge token is flipped over and its effect applied. [Rating: 2/10] Horrible. Nothing new. It's disgusting to see that in 2024 these games are still published.

[Rating: 5/10] As a solo game I found Sfynx just a bit appealing. As a cooperative game it felt more like a hussle. Talking about how to figure out the puzzle took too much time for what the game should be.  Use a few abilities to move a few til in the direction you would like to match certain contract and try to solve all contracts before the game ends.

[Rating: 5/10] I don't really find spatial logic puzzles fun, but I can see the attraction of figuring out the best way to use the special powers and rewards, and the hidden challenge tokens that shift the board make it at least feel more like a game than a straight puzzle.  I really don't like the hieroglyphics - I ended up giving each one a name so I could better remember them.  It says it can play up to 4, but I really don't see the point playing more than 2 at most - seems very prone to alpha player effect and limited communication puzzle coops like The Crew are so so much better.
